items.title: LLMON: An LLM-native Markup Language to Leverage Structure and Semantics at the LLM Interface
items.snippet: This work introduces LLMON (LLM Object Notation), an LLM-native mark-up language designed to communicate the structure and semantic metadata of text to a Large Language Model (LLM) in a natural way. This information can be utilized during model training, prompting, and inference, leading to improvements in accuracy, safety, and security. LLMON addresses the current shortcoming where rich structural and semantic information is often lost when conveyed to LLMs as a simple text string.

items.title: Any Time, Any Space: A World-State-Centric Framework for Agentic Video Generation
items.snippet: This paper presents a world-state-centric framework for long-form agentic video generation, aiming to produce shots that maintain spatial and temporal consistency across nonconsecutive requests. The framework tackles the challenge of translating a screenplay into a coherent video output. This is particularly relevant for creating dynamic and consistent environments in agent-based systems.

items.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
items.snippet: The research explores how computer-use agents can learn to play from synthetic experience, building on their demonstrated capabilities in interpreting screens and executing keyboard and mouse actions. This approach focuses on improving agent performance through simulated environments. It holds promise for developing more versatile and robust AI agents.

items.title: Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
items.snippet: This paper extends on-policy distillation (OPD) with a multi-teacher approach, routing domain-specific data to specialized teachers. The method integrates their capabilities through dense token-level supervision on student-generated trajectories. This aims to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of distilling knowledge from multiple expert models into a single student model.

items.title: The Nature of Swarm Robotics: How New Engineering Methods Are Transforming the Robotics Field
items.snippet: This blog post discusses swarm robotics, an emerging engineering field focused on solving complex challenges by enabling multiple robots to communicate, coordinate, and adapt as a team. It highlights how distributing intelligence across many simple robotic agents allows for sophisticated, adaptive collective behavior. The article emphasizes the resilience and scalability that decentralized swarm systems offer.

items.title: Trust in Depth: Giving agents more autonomy without losing control
items.snippet: This post addresses the challenge of increasing AI agent autonomy while maintaining control, particularly for high-stakes enterprise tasks. It introduces 'Trust in Depth,' a layered approach to ensure agents operate within defined limits and authority. The article emphasizes the importance of agent identity, approval workflows, and scoping agent capabilities to specific job requirements.

items.title: System1-Arena: A Benchmark Suite, Scoring Harness, and Leaderboard for LLM Agents in Closed-Loop Environments
items.snippet: System1-Arena is a new benchmark suite, scoring harness, and leaderboard designed by an academic team to evaluate LLM agents. It includes 52,199 requests across 105 decision kinds in 16 domains, notably featuring 138 closed-loop environments for tasks like web shopping and robotics. The benchmark assesses models on accuracy, Brier score, latency, and cost, providing a comprehensive evaluation of agentic and non-agentic performance.

items.title: What is an LLM agent?
items.snippet: This tutorial defines an LLM agent as an AI system that combines a large language model with planning, memory, and external tools to autonomously complete tasks. Unlike traditional LLMs, agents can make decisions, interact with external systems, and execute multi-step workflows. They are crucial for applications in customer support, software development, and workflow automation.

items.title: LLM-as-a-Judge: The Complete Guide to Run LLM Evals at Scale
items.snippet: This guide provides a comprehensive explanation of LLM-as-a-Judge, detailing how it functions for scalable LLM evaluation. It covers various aspects, including single-output versus pairwise scoring, G-Eval, DAG, and effective prompting techniques. The methodology allows an LLM to act as an automated grader, providing quantitative verdicts or preferences based on defined criteria.

items.title: 16 Best General-Purpose AI Agents in 2026
items.snippet: This roundup reviews the top general-purpose AI agents available in 2026, moving beyond simple chat interfaces to those capable of browsing the web, running code, and completing multi-step tasks. Agents like OpenClaw and Atomic Agent are highlighted for their ability to run tasks locally, remember context, and act across connected tools. The article scores agents on a 36-point rubric, differentiating between conversational assistants and autonomous multi-step action takers.
